/corrections:
Deleted on the founder's instruction: 'delete the route, the page, and all inbound links. Replace it with a single inline Flag this affordance on every protocol page.' The reasoning is that reporting a wrong sentence belongs ON the sentence, not on a destination a reader has to go and find — and the page's own first instruction was false anyway, telling readers to 'use the feedback link on any page' when no prerendered page has ever carried one. NOTHING WAS WITHDRAWN ON EDITORIAL GROUNDS AND NO CONTENT WAS LOST: the full log of 13 substantive corrections moved verbatim to /methodology under

What has already been wrong

, which is also where the landing page's correction count is now read from (correctionLog() in build/prerender.js is the single definition, used by both the composer and assertLandingPage). The URL 301s to /methodology in server.js LEGACY_REDIRECTS, so every external link and bookmark lands on the same content at its new address. Not a 410: the content is still published, at a different URL.
/plan: Removed from the sitemap because Today is a private, device-specific utility surface whose contents depend on local state. It remains served at HTTP 200, self-canonical and noindex,follow so readers can use it and crawlers can follow its links without treating an empty or personal schedule as public editorial content.
/interest: Merged into the home page at the owner's instruction: 'there will no longer be 2 landing pages, just the home page acting as the landing page with the main header as [the interest page's] header.' Its content became the home page. UPDATED 2026-08-09: the landing page was overhauled and the interest FORM, its seven answer panels, the room drawing and the builder drawing were removed on the owner's instruction ('i just need 1 CTA: search and protocol'). The H1, the search-across-five-years drawing, the library drawing and the owner's cause wording all survive, in build/landing.js. POST /api/interest and its table still exist and still work; nothing on any page posts to them, and the /?state= answer handler on "/" is dark because there is no panel left to reveal. The URL 301s to "/" WITH its query string intact (server.js LEGACY_REDIRECTS), so /interest?state=ok&t=<token> — the only copy of a removal token that will ever exist, because nothing here sends email — still lands on the answer it was going to. Not a 410: nothing was withdrawn on editorial or regulatory grounds, and the content is still published, at a different address.
/compare/creatine-monohydrate-vs-sodium-: Sodium Bicarbonate fell from rank 8 to rank 9 of the `muscle` goal when EPO was re-filed into MUSCLE/STRENGTH (commit 3dbf586); the comparison generator pairs a goal's top eight, so this pair stopped being generated. Both compounds are supplements and both pages are still published — nothing was withdrawn on editorial or regulatory grounds. serveMissing() answers 404, not 410, for exactly this reason.

/exercise/Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Rai: Withdrawn from the sitemap on 2026-08-14, hours after being added. Its muscle tag is FALSE — heels fixed, toes lift — dorsiflexion, tagged calves (the antagonist) — so the page was asserting a wrong muscle in its 'Mainly:' line, hyperlinked to that muscle's anatomy page, in its meta description and in its structured data. Indexing it published a confident wrong answer to a search engine and to answer engines at once. Five independent reviewers re-read all fourteen figure-suppressed movements from the instruction text under different lenses and were unanimous on thirteen, 4-1 on Knee_Circles; only these nine were judged false. The other five stay indexed: Posterior_Tibialis_Stretch and Stomach_Vacuum are CORRECTLY tagged and merely too deep to draw, and Rocking_Standing_Calf_Raise, Balance_Board and Ankle_Circles are incomplete rather than untrue — withdrawing those would have been the same error pointing the other way. The page stays served, linked and crawlable, and now states plainly what is wrong with the record. Re-index it only by correcting the tag in the source data, never by editing EX_TAG_AUDIT to say something the instruction text does not support.
